chapter: Becoming a musician: ukulele, clarinet and the Boozaire Kings
title: Crump, the young clarinetist playing High Society
summary: A light-skinned youth called Crump played clarinet and sax at Crescent Star Park but never amounted to much.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: So who were some of the guys that turned out to be musicians along with you when you were growing up?

Well, you'd see them, you'd see all the kids. Well, I didn't pay him no mind, but there was one little youngster, he's about what...about fourteen -- Crump, they called him. ...(?)... Charlie Barbarin's wife; he was his uncle. Crump. He was a little-bitty cat, a little light cat who looked like could be a Spaniard, had pretty black curly hair with big waves in it, and he wore sideburns as a... He didn't have them then, but later on he had these big heavy sideburns. But he played clarinet and saxophone, and I remember going to the Crescent Star Park and I seen him up there with these professional musicians. And he was playing. And they kept featuring him and sending him out for... And he was playing "High Society"; he must have played it about three times during the night. Because this is the hip(?) tune. This is like "Sweet Sue" in New York or "Liza." You played, you know, "High Society." He played

"High Society." And he was celebrated(?). But he didn't ever amount to much as a musician, because at a different level... You could stay, you know, and if you didn't improve, it didn't matter. You were working. But there's still a certain element, and you...
